- Target procurement timeframe: Q4 pilot, then production H1 2027.

- Primary optimization: extensive prefix reuse (shared system + template prompts in workflows) and session-level repetition for end-user chat flows.

What we said we'd follow up with today:
1) Clarify caching assumptions (prefix hit rates vs session/KV cache) and how those translate to effective $/1M observed tokens.
2) Provide a sample TCO calc for the volumes you shared.
3) Share the pricing deck and proposed pilot commitment tiers.

Attachment: redwood-pricing-deck-v3.pdf (pricing tiers, discount schedule, pilot options).

- Aditya: can you put together a short note with hit-rate assumptions and the math for effective $/1M tokens?
- Marcus + I: will draft a pilot proposal (3-month pilot + 30-day evaluation) once we have the final volumes.

Thanks — I’ll hold on formal pricing until we confirm the hit-rate assumptions so the proposal reflects your expected unit economics.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: caching assumptions and effective $/1M tokens (recap + next steps)

Claire — thanks for the export, that helps a lot. Below is a short, pragmatic set of assumptions and the math you can use to map from list price to effective $/1M observed tokens. I kept it conservative and included an optimistic case.

Assumptions (customer profile = template-heavy prompts + frequent repeat sessions):
- Prefix cache (shared system prompts + templates): conservative hit = 25%, expected = 35%, optimistic = 50%.
- Session / KV cache (within active user sessions where the KV cache avoids re-sending KV tokens): conservative additional hit = 5%, expected = 10%, optimistic = 20% (depends on session stickiness).
- Combined effective hit-rate = prefix_hit + session_hit, but note these are not additive across all token types (input vs output). For a simple approximation we use combined_hit = prefix_hit + session_hit (capped at ~60%).

Pricing math (simple):
- Redwood list price (example tier for your volumes / committed pilot): $25 per 1M billable tokens. (We will put exact tiered prices in the proposal; this is illustrative.)
- Observed tokens = 1,000,000 (for 1M observed tokens baseline).
- Billable tokens = Observed_tokens * (1 - combined_hit).
- Cost for 1M observed tokens = $25 * Billable_tokens/1,000,000 = $25 * (1 - combined_hit).
- Effective $/1M observed tokens = $25 * (1 - combined_hit).

Scenarios (per 1M observed tokens):
- Conservative: combined_hit = 30% (25% prefix + 5% session) -> effective = $25 * 0.70 = $17.50 / 1M observed tokens.
- Expected: combined_hit = 45% (35% prefix + 10% session) -> effective = $25 * 0.55 = $13.75 / 1M observed tokens.
- Optimistic: combined_hit = 60% (50% prefix + 10% session or 40%+20%) -> effective = $25 * 0.40 = $10.00 / 1M observed tokens.

Notes / caveats:
- The above is a simplification: input vs output token mix matters (we bill per-token served by the model). If most of the repeated prefixes are input-only, that reduces billable input tokens but not necessarily output tokens. We can refine with the CSV distribution you sent.
- For stateful chat, KV cache can be very effective for long-running sessions, but it requires the runtime to keep session state (we support session-level KV caching in Redwood Dedicated/Private).
- Additional levers: batching, quantization profile, and model selection. Those reduce compute cost but won’t change the per-token billing unless you put cached artifacts in front of the model (e.g., rerank/candidates replaced by a cheaper service).

Illustrative monthly $ impact at 1.5B observed tokens (use expected hit = 45%):
- Billable tokens = 1.5B * (1 - 0.45) = 825M billable tokens.
- Cost = 825 * ($25 per 1M) = $20,625 (i.e., 825 * 25 = 20625 in thousands? Clarify units below) -> Wait, better expressed: 825M / 1M * $25 = 825 * $25 = $20,625 (USD).
- Effective per-1M observed = $13.75 (same as per-1M calc above).

If your budget target is ~$10 / 1M observed tokens, we should be looking at either:
- Increasing cache hit to ~60%+ (optimistic scenario), or
- Negotiating a lower list price at higher committed volumes / longer term (example: $18 / 1M list price at annual commitment), or
- A hybrid: moderate list-price discount + modest 50% hit.

Next steps I can take now:
- I’ll run your CSV through a quick estimator and send a refined hit-rate recommendation (conservative/expected/optimistic) by tomorrow morning.
- If you want formal TCO, we’ll produce a short spreadsheet showing per-tier costs, pilot commitment options, and model variant recommendations.

-TL;DR: With a $25 list price and expected combined hit ~45%, you land in the mid-$13s per 1M observed tokens. To get to ~$10/1M you need ~60% combined hit or a lower list price via a commitment.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
